## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences heart-related issues, including a possible congenital heart defect requiring regular check-ups.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, ranging from valve changes to hole in the heart chambers.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences constipation issues, which can be frustrating at times.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Constipation is a common issue among people with KBG syndrome, affecting approximately 20-40% of affected individuals.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences hypotonia, which affects her muscle tone, leading to stiffness and requiring therapeutic interventions.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Hypotonia is a common feature in KBG syndrome, affecting approximately 30% of affected individuals.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has palatal abnormalities that require close monitoring with her healthcare team.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Palatal abnormalities are a common feature in KBG syndrome, affecting approximately 10% of affected individuals.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences vision problems, including myopia and hypermetropia, and occasional squinting.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Vision problems are a common feature in KBG syndrome, affecting approximately 20-40% of affected individuals.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tooth sensitivity, particularly with cold foods, indicating potential dental issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Tooth sensitivity is a common feature in KBG syndrome, affecting approximately 20-40% of affected individuals.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences delays in reaching developmental milestones and requires additional support in school.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Delayed development is a common feature in KBG syndrome, affecting approximately 30% of affected individuals.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences behavioral differences, including autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, and anxiety.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Behavioral differences are a common feature in KBG syndrome, affecting approximately 30% of affected individuals.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has brachydactyly, a shortened fifth finger, and an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Skeletal anomalies are a common feature in KBG syndrome, affecting approximately 10% of affected individuals.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Screening for heart defects: Regular heart check-ups are recommended due to a familial history of cardiac issues.
b) Monitoring vision: Regular hearing reviews should begin at age 5, even if earlier reviews provide a clear response.
c) Management of constipation: Ensuring proper hydration and dietary adjustments can help alleviate constipation issues.
d) Speech therapy: Children with KBG syndrome may experience speech delay, and speech therapy is recommended to address this.
e) Orthopedic evaluation: Regular orthopedic evaluations are advised to monitor the patient's skeletal development and address any issues.
f) Neurological assessment: Regular neurological assessments are recommended to monitor the patient's brain function and manage hypotonia.
g) Ophthalmologic evaluation: Regular ophthalmologic evaluations are recommended to monitor vision and address any palatal abnormalities.

j) Refer for physical therapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavior therapy if developmental delays are observed.
